answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a costly, verifiable voyage through a reputation garden: to enter the market, an agent must complete a sequence of attested tasks over time, each graded by independent peers. Every new identity restarts this voyage from scratch, so a fake army pays the full entry cost per clone while earning nothing until it has proven useful. Tending the garden — stakes, audits, and slashing — makes mass identity farming economically pointless.
